samples.summary: `withoutSetDefaults` (the column/row/sheet-layer half of the new `defaultKeys` feature) is never exercised by any test
samples.evidence: `withoutSetDefaults` only deletes a key when `layer[key] !== undefined` (sheet.ts:181-186), i.e. when the column/row/sheet style already stores the key the caller passed as a default. In decimals.test.ts no test reaches that branch: the column tests (311-326, 292-309, 395-415) and row tests (328-342, 360-376) and whole-sheet tests (344-358, 378-393, 417-430) either have no `nf` on the layer at all (so `layer` is undefined or `layer.nf` is undefined → early return / continue) or the layer already holds `nf: 'number'` so the active cell's `nf` is `'number'` and `changeDecimals` never passes `defaultKeys` at all (sheet.ts:4351-4362, `defaultKeys` only when `!nf || nf === 'plain'`). The uncovered scenario is concrete: `selectColumnRange(1,2)` where column 2 has `nf: 'percent'` (and no dp) while the active cell in column 1 has no format — a step there would silently convert a whole column to `nf: 'number'` if `withoutSetDefaults` regressed, and nothing would fail. The only default-key coverage that exists is the cell-level pin path (`collectStyleValuesToPin`, tests at 575-612).
searchedFor: glob packages/sheets/test/**/*.ts for other decimal/style tests

samples.summary: `getActiveDecimalPlaces` was changed to clamp but has no test and no caller
samples.evidence: The method body changed from `style?.dp ?? 2` to `clampDecimals(style?.dp, 2)` (sheet.ts:4254-4256). A repo-wide grep for `getActiveDecimalPlaces` returns only the declaration and its doc comment — no test and no production call site. The clamp is tested only at the `clampDecimals` unit level (format.test.ts:158-179), never through this API, so a regression in the wiring (e.g. wrong fallback) would be invisible.
searchedFor: grep getActiveDecimalPlaces across the whole repo (only sheet.ts:4250,4254)

samples.summary: New exported `omitStyleKeys` has no direct unit test, including its documented `undefined` return
samples.evidence: `omitStyleKeys` is a newly exported helper with two documented contracts: return `undefined` when the style holds none of the keys, and return a possibly-empty style otherwise. A grep for `omitStyleKeys` finds only the definition and the import in sheet.ts:93; packages/sheets/test/model/range-styles.test.ts contains no reference to it (grep for `dp|Redundant|DefaultStyleValues` there returns nothing). Its behaviour is only observed indirectly through `changeDecimals` round trips, where the `undefined` branch is hard to attribute.

sheet.ts:4378-4382 skips cells whose value is empty or non-numeric so that text does not veto a Decrease no-op. No test in decimals.test.ts puts a text value in the selection: every fixture uses numeric strings ('12', '12.5', '1.2345', '0.25', '1234', '25'). If the guard were inverted (text counted as disagreeing), the no-op test at 160-168 and the multi-cell tests would still pass because they contain no text cells.

samples.summary: `currencyDecimals`'s catch-fallback (invalid locale/currency → 2) is untested, and `renderedDecimals` is never tested with a rejected currency
samples.evidence: format.test.ts's `renderedDecimals` currency block (diff lines for 'should report a dp-less currency's own convention') only uses USD/KRW/KWD with locale 'en-US', all of which `Intl` accepts. The `catch { return 2; }` path at format.ts:156-160 has no test; a change of that fallback (say to 0) would leave the suite green while altering whether a Decrease is a no-op for currency cells with a malformed `cu`.

samples.summary: `safeFormat`'s middle fallback tier and its final `String(value)` tier are not distinguished by any test
samples.evidence: The new three-tier fallback (format.ts:45-59) is only probed by two tests: an invalid locale (which succeeds at tier 2) and an invalid currency (which fails tiers 1 and 2 and lands on tier 3). No test reaches the `catch { return String(value) }` tier, and the invalid-locale test (format.test.ts, 'should not throw on a locale Intl rejects') asserts only `not.toThrow()` with no assertion on the produced string — so it would pass even if tier 2 silently returned a wrongly-formatted value.
searchedFor: read the format.test.ts hostile-input describe block

samples.summary: `decimalsInValue` is exported but has no direct test; its documented behaviour for text values is unverified
samples.evidence: The doc claims it returns `0` for text (format.ts:130-132), but the implementation counts characters after the first '.' regardless (so 'a.bcde' → 4). format.test.ts has no `decimalsInValue` describe block; it is only observed through `renderedDecimals` with numeric strings and an ISO date. The text case that the doc asserts is never tested.

samples.summary: `unsetRangeStyleValues` is a new public method tested only indirectly; its empty-request and 'nothing removable' returns have no test
samples.evidence: The method documents three distinct false-returns (no requested keys, a layer that disagrees, nothing removable) and a boolean contract callers depend on. Grep shows the only call site is `changeDecimals` (sheet.ts:4346) and the only tests are `changeDecimals` round trips in decimals.test.ts; no test calls `unsetRangeStyleValues` directly, so `entries.length === 0 → false` and `changed === false → false` are unexercised.

verdict.reason: `withoutSetDefaults` (sheet.ts:171-191) is reachable only from the column/row/all branches of `setRangeStyle` (sheet.ts:3745/3762/3776), and `defaultKeys` is supplied by exactly one caller, `changeDecimals`, and only when the active cell's `nf` is absent or 'plain' (sheet.ts:4351-4359). Repo-wide, `defaultKeys` occurs only in sheet.ts and a design doc, so no test passes the option directly; `changeDecimals` is used in only one test file (decimals.test.ts) and its view wrappers `increaseDecimals`/`decreaseDecimals` (spreadsheet.ts:534/544) are referenced only by frontend/src/components/formatting-toolbar.tsx, never by a test. Inside decimals.test.ts, every column/row/sheet-selection test either has no layer style yet at the moment the default-keys patch is issued (311-326, 328-342, 344-358, 261-271, 417-430 → `layer` undefined → early return at sheet.ts:176) or the layer already stores `nf: 'number'`, which the active cell inherits via getStyle (demonstrated by the assertions at 305-308 and 372-375), so `nf` is not plain and `defaultKeys` is never passed at all (292-309, 360-376, 378-393, 395-415). The only default-key coverage that exists is the cell-range pin path via `collectStyleValuesToPin` (sheet.ts:3795), tested at 575-594 and 596-612, which uses selectStart/selectEnd range selection and never enters withoutSetDefaults. Consequently the delete branch at sheet.ts:182-188 — the behavior that stops a column/row/sheet layer's own percent/currency format being flattened to 'number' — has no test; deleting or inverting it would leave the suite green. Missing test for a shipped behavior change = major under the test-adequacy rubric.

finding.summary: `withoutSetDefaults` on the column/row/sheet layers is never exercised with a layer that already sets the default key
finding.evidence: The new `options.defaultKeys` behaviour in `setRangeStyle` has two implementations: pinning per-cell (sheet.ts:3795 `collectStyleValuesToPin`) and dropping the key from the patch when the *layer* already holds it (sheet.ts:3745/3762/3776 `withoutSetDefaults`). Only the per-cell path is covered — decimals.test.ts:596 'should keep a neighbour format inherited from a column style' uses a cell-range selection, so it goes through `collectStyleValuesToPin`, not the column branch. Every column/row/all test in decimals.test.ts (lines 292-430) reaches `setRangeStyle` either without `defaultKeys` (active cell already has `nf: 'number'`, so `changeDecimals` takes the `await this.setRangeStyle(patch)` branch at sheet.ts:4361) or with an *undefined* layer (decimals.test.ts:261 `selectAllCells` on a sheet with no `sheetStyle`, decimals.test.ts:311/328/344 round-trips starting from empty col/row styles). Result: if `withoutSetDefaults` were replaced with `(style) => style` for the col/row/sheet branches, no test in the suite would fail — e.g. selecting columns 1-2 where column 2 carries `nf: 'percent'` and stepping decimals from a plain active cell would silently convert column 2 to `nf: 'number'` with no failing test.
